correctionReason: A later audit compared the dashboard against the actual deterministic Mitchell output. Therefore closeness between dashboard A and B cannot establish source adherence. The prior raw-pose topology fail was too harsh, but treating the same dashboard as a factual-positive-control was also too strong.
scope: The exact source and actual deterministic research render are authoritative evidence. Text, metrics, PASS labels, regenerated source depictions and regenerated control images inside producer reports are non-authoritative.
currentObservations: The aa89f137 embedded candidate is visually much more discreet and realistic than the later fantasy roller/rail prototype.
The dashboard's own A/B comparison is not a valid fidelity comparison because A is not the actual deterministic research output.
The candidate may be close enough to ordinary real slide hardware to pass unnoticed at normal catalog scale, but factual H45 identity remains unverified.

negativeControlContrast.description: Later outputs repeatedly collapse to an obviously invented roller/rail archetype with fantasy mechanical features.
negativeControlContrast.researchUse: Compare the discreet aa89f137 regime against the fantasy archetype to investigate reference binding and context-driven mode switching; neither is currently a verified faithful master.

researchConsequence: A producer-generated dashboard must never be allowed to regenerate its own control/reference and then use internal A/B similarity as fidelity evidence.
Normal-size plausibility remains insufficient for factual product imagery.
Pose-invariant landmark review remains necessary, but only against exact source evidence or a deterministic derivative whose provenance is external to the producer.
The next question is what causes the large switch between discreet generic-hardware synthesis and fantasy prototype substitution.
